title: Did the Gran Sasso Experiment Rule Out the Diósi-Penrose Theory? Musing on the 2021 Result and the Present Experimental Status
authors: Catalina Curceanu, Nicola Bortolotti, Lajos Diósi, Simone Manti, Kristian Piscicchia
abstract: In 2021, a low-background experiment at the Gran Sasso National Laboratory searched for spontaneous radiation predicted by the standard Markovian Diósi-Penrose (DP) dynamics and obtained the new bound $R_0 > 5.4 \times 10^{-11}\,\mathrm{m}$ at $95\%$ probability for the short-length cutoff parameter. For germanium at the experimental temperature, the parameter-free prescription identifying $R_0$ with the spatial quantum spread of a nucleus gives $R_0 \simeq 5 \times 10^{-12}\,\mathrm{m}$. That particular combination, Diósi's stochastic dynamics and the Penrose-motivated mass-density resolution, was therefore excluded. Subsequent searches strengthened the cutoff bound. The Majorana Demonstrator improved it in 2022, and XENONnT has now obtained the world-leading limits $R_0 > 4.9 \times 10^{-10}\,\mathrm{m}$ at $90\%$ confidence level and $R_0 > 4.5 \times 10^{-10}\,\mathrm{m}$ at $95\%$ confidence level. These advances reinforce the 2021 exclusion but do not alter its logical scope: they \emph{parametrically constrain} the Markovian, effectively white-noise DP dynamics, not Penrose's (and Diósi's) lifetime criterion independently of a dynamics, and not all colored-noise, dissipative, or otherwise modified gravity-related spontaneous collapse theories. We reconstruct what Gran Sasso did and did not rule out and place that conclusion in the present experimental context.
summary: This paper reviews the experimental status of the Diósi-Penrose theory of spontaneous wave function collapse using results from low-background detectors. While the 2021 Gran Sasso result provided an initial exclusion, the authors clarify that modern, stronger bounds only constrain the specific Markovian dynamics used, leaving other collapse theories potentially untouched.
main_problem: The paper addresses whether the Gran Sasso experiment successfully ruled out the Diósi-Penrose (DP) theory of spontaneous wave-function collapse.
main_result: The 2021 result excluded the parameter-free version of the theory under specific assumptions, but subsequent, stronger bounds from experiments like XENONnT only constrain the Markovian dynamics, not the entire theoretical framework.
method: The authors analyze experimental constraints by comparing measured low-background radiation counts against theoretical predictions derived from the DP model.
model_or_system: The model is the Diósi-Penrose theory, which posits spontaneous collapse governed by a stochastic dynamics dependent on a spatial cutoff parameter, $R_0$. Experiments utilize low-background detectors at facilities like Gran Sasso and XENONnT.
key_observables: The primary observable is the absence of a statistically significant excess spontaneous radiation signal in the energy range of 1.0–3.8 MeV (Gran Sasso) or 1–140 keV (XENONnT).
important_parameters: The key parameter is the spatial cutoff $R_0$, with current world-leading bounds exceeding $4.5 	imes 10^{-10}$ m.
main_assumptions: The exclusion is strictly limited to the Markovian, white-noise dynamics of the DP model and does not constrain colored-noise or other modified gravity collapse theories.
figures_summary: Figure 1 compares the lower bounds on $R_0$ derived from Gran Sasso, Majorana, and XENONnT experiments, illustrating the tightening experimental constraints.
paper_structure: The paper reconstructs the scope of the 2021 Gran Sasso result, updates this understanding with the latest XENONnT bounds, and clarifies the precise theoretical limitations of the exclusion.
why_interesting: It is highly relevant as it discusses fundamental issues in quantum foundations—the measurement problem—by interpreting cutting-edge experimental constraints on spontaneous collapse models.
